en.title: Fewest Uniform Subtractions of a Valid Positive Number to Reach Zero
en.description:
In a non-negative array, each step chooses a positive integer x no greater than the current smallest non-zero element and subtracts x from every positive element; elements equal to 0 stay 0. Find the minimum number of steps to make every element zero.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the array. 1≤n≤100, 0≤element≤100.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 0 and 1. Repeated equal positive values reach zero in the same operation.
hints: Count the distinct positive values; 0 does not count.
